headline: 28th Amendment Passes: Corponations Granted Sovereign Status on U.S. Soil
body:
The Federal Remnant Senate ratified the 28th Amendment to the Constitution today by a margin of 61 to 39, formally granting recognized corponations the legal status of sovereign entities within designated territorial zones. The measure, debated for nearly seven years, rewrites the relationship between what remains of the federal government and the twelve corponations that have lobbied aggressively for the designation. Axiom, Tessera, and Sterling-Nakamura were the first to sign territorial acknowledgment agreements in what officials in the Capital District are calling a 'managed transition of governance.'

Critics are not calling it that. Senator Dorinda Achebe-Mares, one of the amendment's loudest opponents, addressed the chamber floor for forty-one minutes before the final vote. 'We are not managing a transition,' she said. 'We are signing a surrender.' Protests erupted within hours in the Gray Zone and The Narrows, where residents fear the amendment strips them of federal civil protections they technically still hold. the Gray Zone Voice estimates crowds of over 80,000 gathered at the GLMZ Federal Administrative Plaza by nightfall.

Corponation representatives celebrated with unusual public visibility. Axiom's Chief Sovereignty Officer, Remington Johal-Brennan, released a statement calling the amendment 'the honest acknowledgment of a reality that has existed for decades.' Ironclad and Arcturus Defense have already submitted expanded territorial boundary proposals to the newly formed Sovereignty Arbitration Bureau. The Federal Remnant, reduced to handling border disputes and ratifying corporate applications, now administers fewer than 12% of GLMZ's residential zones.
aftermath: Within eighteen months, six corponations had filed competing boundary claims over The Circuit's central interchange district, triggering the first formal Sovereignty Arbitration proceeding and a years-long legal deadlock that left large swaths of the district in administrative limbo.
runner_relevance: The 28th Amendment created enforcement gaps at every newly drawn territorial boundary — corponations could not legally police beyond their own zones, and the Federal Remnant lacked the manpower to cover the rest. Runners immediately began taking border-zone courier contracts, moving sensitive documents and physical assets across disputed territories where no single security force had jurisdiction. Protection contracts spiked as small businesses in boundary zones lost access to any recognized law enforcement. Extraction contracts emerged as individuals trapped in newly designated corporate territories sought to relocate to neutral ground.
